scenario.name: Docker Security, CNCF Falco & MITRE — Container Mounted /var/run/docker.sock Unix Socket Escalation Audit
scenario.overview: Think of a classic neighborhood post office with brass P.O. boxes lining the back wall, a parcel scale counter, a blue street mailbox outside, and angled mail sorting chutes. At the neighborhood post office counter, a sender slips tiny coded lines onto the back of ordinary postcards and drops them one by one into the mail sorting slot. In this real-world scenario, the intruder bypasses the normal inspection rule to reach the brass p.o. box sorting wall, then bypasses the normal inspection rule to reach the brass p.o. box sorting wall. The postmaster reviews the evening dispatch ledger and spots hundreds of oddly coded postcards all mailed to the exact same remote P.O. box. In this scenario (T1613, Docker Security, CNCF Falco & MITRE, Container Mounted /var/run/docker.sock Unix Socket Escalation Audit), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: discovering Mounted /var/run/docker.sock, then spawning Sibling Container with HostPID, then entering Host PID 1 Mount. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Discovering Mounted /var/run/docker.sock, then Spawning Sibling Container with HostPID, then Entering Host PID 1 Mount, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection pivots on auditd Event 42 correlated across the documented kill chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: Discovering Mounted /var/run/docker.sock Inside Container Mount Table
stages.subtitle: Discovery (T1613 - Container and Resource Discovery)
stages.description: At the neighborhood post office counter, a sender slips tiny coded lines onto the back of ordinary postcards and drops them one by one into the mail sorting slot. Specifically in Step 1, the intruder bypasses the normal inspection rule to reach the brass p.o. box sorting wall while everyday visitors and the postal clerk go about their routine. After gaining code execution inside a build or agent container, the actor inspects /proc/self/mountinfo (or runs find / -name docker.sock) and discovers the writable host Unix domain socket /var/run/docker.sock mounted from /run/docker.sock (logged in Linux Audit Event 42 with SocketFamily=AF_UNIX , /var/run/docker.sock, AuditRuleKey=docker_socket_access, CallerProcess=/usr/bin/curl , Container Cgroup so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes grep docker.sock /proc/self/mountinfo (which executes a Kubernetes API request or container runtime command , grep docker.sock /proc/self/mountinfo configuring pod security contexts, volume mo so that breaks out of container cgroup/namespace isolation , T1613 during "Discovering Mounted /var/run/docker.sock Inside Container Mount Table" to gain unrestricted root execution on the underlying Kubernetes worker node and access host credentials , kubelet / systemd). Next, the follow-up artifact ls -la /var/run/docker.sock runs (which executes a Kubernetes API request or container runtime command , ls -la /var/run/docker.sock configuring pod security contexts, volume mounts , hos so that breaks out of container cgroup/namespace isolation , T1613 during "Discovering Mounted /var/run/docker.sock Inside Container Mount Table" to gain unrestricted root execution on the underlying Kubernetes worker node and access host credentials , kubelet / systemd). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ curl --unix-socket /var/run/docker.sock http://localhost/info / ⇠#1 ACK 42) from Node ① (#1 Compromised CI/CD Container) to Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Host Namespace (--pid=host nsenter)).

keySpecs.value: Replace Docker-in-Docker (/var/run/docker.sock mounts) in CI/CD pipelines with rootless image builders such as Kaniko, Buildah, or Sysbox user-namespace isolation.

stages.title: Stage 2: Spawning Sibling Container with HostPID, HostNetwork & Privileged Mode via Unix Socket
stages.subtitle: Privilege Escalation (T1611 - Escape to Host)
stages.description: Because each postcard carries valid postage and a harmless street address, the postal clerk stamps them smoothly and sends them down the brass sorting chute. Here in Step 2 inside the post office, the intruder bypasses the normal inspection rule to reach the brass p.o. box sorting wall without disturbing the registered certified mail safe. Sending an HTTP POST request over /var/run/docker.sock to http://localhost/v1.43/containers/create, the actor instructs the host dockerd daemon to launch a sibling container configured with PidMode="host", NetworkMode="host", and Privileged=true (logged in Linux Audit Event 201 with NamespaceSharing=PidMode=host, NetworkMode=host, PrivilegedMode=true, SocketTransport=unix:///var/run/docker.sock so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes ausearch -k docker_socket_access -i (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , ausearch -k docker_socket_access -i via System / Runtime Execution Interface, passing the ex so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1611 during "Spawning Sibling Container with HostPID, HostNetwork & Privileged Mode via Unix Socket" , Sending an HTTP POST request over /var/run/docker while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact docker events --since 1h --filter "event=create" runs (which executes a Kubernetes API request or container runtime command , docker events --since 1h --filter "event=create" configuring pod security contexts so that breaks out of container cgroup/namespace isolation , T1611 during "Spawning Sibling Container with HostPID, HostNetwork & Privileged Mode via Unix Socket" to gain unrestricted root execution on the underlying Kubernetes worker node and access host credentials , kubelet / systemd). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ POST /v1.43/containers/create (PidMode=host, NetworkMode=host, Privileged=true) / ⇠#2 ACK 201) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 Mounted /var/run/docker.sock (AF_UNIX)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Host Namespace (--pid=host nsenter)).

keySpecs.value: If a monitoring container requires read-only Docker metadata, place a read-only socket proxy (such as Tecnativa docker-socket-proxy) in front of /var/run/docker.sock that blocks POST /containers/create and /exec.

stages.title: Stage 3: Entering Host PID 1 (systemd) Mount & IPC Namespaces via nsenter
stages.subtitle: Escape to Host (T1611 - Escape to Host)
stages.description: One harmless postcard at a time, an entire confidential binder is smuggled right out of the post office without ever raising the heavy parcel-inspection alarm. In this final step inside the post office, the intruder bypasses the normal inspection rule to reach the brass p.o. box sorting wall until the postmaster dispatch ledger catches the mismatch. Next, the follow-up artifact ls -l /proc/1/ns/ runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , ls -l /proc/1/ns/ via System / Runtime Execution Interface, passing the exact arguments, tar so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1611 during "Entering Host PID 1 , systemd Mount & IPC Namespaces via nsenter" , Because the sibling container shares the host PID namespace , --pid=host and runs with CAP_SYS_ADMIN, it invokes nsenter --target 1 --mount --uts --ipc --net --pid to attach directly to all Linux namespaces of host PID 1 , systemd while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ nsenter --target 1 --mount --uts --ipc --net --pid -- /bin/bash / ⇠#3 ACK 308) from Node ③ (#3 Mounted /var/run/docker.sock (AF_UNIX)) to Node ④ (#4 Host dockerd Daemon (root)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Host Namespace (--pid=host nsenter)).
